records.text: A “road Closure” or “full Road Closure” shall be defined as the blockage and/or restriction of a roadway from civilians and/or individuals who are not essential to the given situation or circumstance(s). The individual(s) who are restricted from the closed roadway shall be designated at the discretion of the individual leading or commanding the circumstance/situation/incident that caused the road closure.

A “road closure” shall also include the partial restriction and/or blockage of a roadway. Any government authority authorized by this section to initiate a road closure may initiate a partial road closure instead. The term “Road Closure” shall also include a partial road closure any time it is referenced in this section.
A “partial road closure” shall be defined as a road closure that does not require a detour and still allows two-way travel on the partially closed road.

The term “roadway," “road,” or "highway" includes a common and public highway, street, avenue, parkway, driveway, square, place, bridge, viaduct or trestle, any part of which is intended for or used for the passage of vehicles and includes the area between the lateral property lines thereof.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to execute the closure of certain roads, either in the support of a law enforcement closure or for maintenance and repair to road infrastructure.
Law enforcement officers execute road closures for:
(a) The preservation of a crime scene
(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority
(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

(e) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or endanger the lives of responding officers, or hinder the ability to combat crime
(f) Situation where the flow of traffic on a roadway near the situation may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel.
Fire/Rescue personnel may execute road closures for:
(a) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or patients
(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority
(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.
Fire/Rescue Services at the Municipal and County levels may also execute the closure of certain roads in connection with active fire/rescue scenes, training, or operations.
Medical services, both private and government-owned, may close off the immediate area, including roads, connected to a medical call or situation.
Specific roads or streets may be closed for government events or training at the direction of a Department Head or Governor.

Civilians wishing to host an assembly, event, or demonstration may, with or without connection to a protest permit, request for the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority to order the closure of certain roads connected to said assembly, event, or demonstration.

Any person who stands on any equipment placed on or near any highway with the textual markings containing "POLICE" that could or may obstruct the efficacy of the equipment shall be guilty of Obstruction of Justice.

The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall have the authority to execute the closure of roads going one-hundred-fifty (150) studs before, or across, through, or around any tunnel or bridge under their administration, or anywhere else where it requires, for maintenance or upkeep of public infrastructure, or any other scene relating to their official duties, that being a fire, rescue, or medical scene.

(a) Should the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission need to establish a closure on a roadway or state highway more than one-hundred-fifty (150) studs before or around any tunnel or bridge they gain authorization pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1102.

The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee, shall be responsible for publishing a road closures handbook, which may be aesthetically renamed, that promulgates the rules and regulations for conducting road closures, partial road closure, checkpoints, or modifying the speed limit on a public road, as decided by the Secretary of Transportation.
(a) The road closures handbook must contain rules about, but shall not be limited to include:
(i) Placing signage that warns drivers about road closures ahead;
(ii) Placing signage that warns drivers about changed road conditions on the road ahead; and
(iii) Placing signage that notifies drivers when a road closure or changed road condition has ended.
(b) Any authority that is authorized to conduct a road closure or partial road closure must comply with this handbook.
(c) The Secretary of Transportation may direct the Mayflower Transportation Police to issue citations or arrest any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook.
Any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook shall be liable to be issued a citation or arrested for 2 M.S.C. § 1211 “Obstruction of Traffic”.

records.text: The Department of Transportation shall incorporate a subordinate agency (hereinafter “Mayflower Transportation Police”, “Transportation Police”, “agency”, or “MTP”); which shall be the principal law enforcement and protective entity of the Department of Transportation.

The Secretary of Transportation shall have direct supervision of the Mayflower Transportation Police and appoint a Chief of Police, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the oversight and management of the agency.
(a) The Chief of Police of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall create recruitment, training, and employment procedures within the service.
The Mayflower Transportation Police shall:

(a) Enforce and/or investigate elements of the criminal code (Title 1 of the M.S.C.) and elements of the vehicle code (title 2 of the M.S.C.), subject to the limitation that at least one of the following criteria must be met:
(i) The offender endangers or harms Department of Transportation (including subordinate agency) personnel or a person utilizing Department of Transportation (including subordinate agency) services.
(ii) The offense was committed against, in relation to, or under the purview of the Department of Transportation or any of its subordinate agencies.

(iii) The offense was committed within or in eyesight of any of the following: property or infrastructure owned, maintained, or administered by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies (e.g., MTA, MAA); official operations or events conducted by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies; MTA bus stops; MTA bus routes; or road closures managed by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies.
(iv) The offense relates to a motor vehicle accident or a commercial vehicle.
(v) A Transportation Police officer witnesses a felony offense or an offense that poses a significant danger to the general public or a threat to public safety.
(vi) A Transportation Police officer is participating in an inter-agency task force or any other similar assignment; or is providing assistance to another law enforcement agency.
(vii) A State of Emergency is declared.
(b) Provide protective and/or security services to the Department of Transportation and its subordinate agencies.
(c) Have the principal jurisdiction to investigate any motor vehicle accident on any roadway in the state. This jurisdiction is subordinate only to the Mayflower State Police.

(d) Have the authority to conduct commercial vehicle enforcement functions, including conducting commercial vehicle inspections and establishing commercial vehicle checkpoints. This authority is subordinate only to the Mayflower State Police.
(e) Overall ensure public safety, support the Department of Transportation, and collaborate with other law enforcement and public safety agencies to support the agency’s duties.

(i) Transportation Police officers shall have the authority to assist other peace officers who request assistance. This includes but is not limited to “10-58”, “58” (or its equivalent, e.g., panic buttons) calls on the radio or when Transportation Police assistance is specifically requested.

(ii) Transportation Police officers shall have the authority to engage in pursuits if an offender flees from MTP police or security officers who are actively attempting to detain or arrest an individual, given the aforementioned criteria for enforcing the criminal or vehicle code are met; or if assisting other peace officers as per this act.
(f) Perform any other reasonable duties or functions at the discretion of the Secretary of Transportation and/or Chief of Police.
Police Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall:
(a) Have peace officer status and possess all the authorities, powers, privileges, and responsibilities of any other peace officer, in addition to those granted by this legislation.

(b) Be considered employees of the Department of Transportation. For the purposes of employment limits, persons employed by the Department of Transportation and the agency shall have both positions count as one specific employment position.
Security Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall:
(a) Not hold peace officer status nor be classified as private security officers. However, shall:

(i) Be granted the powers, authorities, and privileges afforded to private security officers under the Security Services Act. This includes but is not limited to being designated as an "authorized officer."
(ii) Be authorized, in accordance with department guidelines, to issue citations for the following offenses under the Mayflower State Code:
(1) 1 M.S.C. § 1314 “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”
(2) 1 M.S.C. § 4107 “Violation of MTA Rules of Conduct”
(3) Any other offense under the direction of a peace officer. Such citations shall be issued on behalf of the peace officer rather than the security officer.
(iii) Be authorized, in accordance with department guidelines, to operate emergency vehicles and utilize emergency lights and sirens.

(b) Be considered employees of the Department of Transportation. For the purposes of employment limits persons employed by the Department of Transportation and the agency shall have both positions count as one specific employment position.
DEFINITIONS. A “residential roadway” shall be defined as a road within a residential neighbourhood.
An “urban roadway” shall be defined as a road within a city limit.
A “rural roadway” shall be defined as a roadway outside of a city limit.
SPEED LIMITS. Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a residential roadway shall be 30 mph.
Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of an urban roadway shall be 50 mph.
Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a rural roadway shall be 70 mph.

records.text: LONG TITLE. An act to ensure that checkpoints in the state are established and precedents are set up for departmental leadership to start doing checkpoints.
SHORT TITLE. This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Mayflower Checkpoint Act.”
The term “checkpoint” or “checking station” shall refer to the following:

(a) Barriers set up to block traffic by law enforcement to check for BOLOs, warrants, firearms licenses, or driver’s licenses, or for commercial vehicle officers to conduct commercial vehicle inspections.
The term “commercial vehicle officer” shall refer to the following:
(a) Any member of the state police’s commercial vehicle enforcement task force, otherwise known as CVE.
(b) An Officer of the Mayflower Transportation Police designated as such by the Chief of Police or his designee(s).
The term “commercial vehicle inspection” shall refer to the following:
(a) The inspection (search) of cargo, shipping documents, and commercial driver’s license(s).
The term “natural resources inspection” shall refer to the following:
(a) The inspection (search) of fish, lumber, fishing license(s), and lumber license(s).

Commercial vehicle officers of the state police shall have the ability to establish checkpoints on any public roadway and establish checkpoints on state highways for the purpose of conducting commercial vehicle inspections.
(a) The state police shall have the sole authority and power to establish checkpoints on state highways, unless an agency has proper authority from the colonel of the state police to establish one.

Any municipal or county law enforcement agency shall have the ability to establish checking stations on any municipal or county roadway within their administration for the purpose of checking driver’s license(s).

The National Guard shall have the ability to establish checkpoints anywhere within a Military Exclusion Zone or on any road directly adjacent to a Mayflower National Guard installation with the authorization from a Senior Officer or Command Group Personnel. During a deployment by the governor, the National Guard shall have the ability to establish a checkpoint on any roadway or state highway within the deployment area. Military police must be present for all established checkpoints.

Each department stated above shall set up its own internal regulations on how checkpoints or checking stations shall be established, which shall not contradict but further expand upon these provisions.
To prevent the unnecessary halt of members of the public, a vehicle shall only be stopped at a checkpoint or checking station for a maximum of five (5) minutes, unless the following are met:
(a) there is an active threat to the checkpoint or checking station;
(b) the vehicle is subject to a commercial vehicle or natural resource inspection; and
(c) a peace officer or member of the national guard, with reasonable suspicion of a crime, orders the individual to exit their vehicle.
The Port Authority Police Department may set up checkpoints anywhere on Port Authority Installations, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110.
“Checkpoint(s)” shall refer to barriers set up to block traffic by Law Enforcement Officers or Guardsmen to check for BOLOs, warrants, driver licenses, and firearm licenses.

Any person who fails to provide identification or property documentation for a vehicle or themselves to law enforcement, or members of the national guard, or conservation officers at a checkpoint or checking station shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. 1 § 1305 Failure to Comply.
"Bridge" shall be defined as:

(a) A lawful bridge over navigable waters of the Union of Columbia, including approaches, fenders, and appurtenances thereto, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying railroad traffic, or both railroad and highway traffic, or if a State, county, municipality, or other political subdivision is the owner or joint owner thereof, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying highway traffic.
The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall be responsible for maintenance, upkeep, and administration of all tunnels and bridges within the state.

(a) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall additionally be responsible for all firefighting, rescue, and medical efforts and operations on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(b) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall contract private companies/entities, or request other government agencies, to assist with or complete certain maintenance-related tasks on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(c) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall, with the consent of the Governor of the State of Mayflower, officially name any tunnel or bridge under its administration, and must notify the public of the change through forms of public documentation or notification, such as a letter or press release.
(d) The Port Authority’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occurring within any tunnel or bridge under its administration.
"Tunnel" shall be defined as:
(a) An underground, underwater, or undersea passageway which is used and operated for the purposes of vehicle, pedestrian, or railroad traffic, or any combination of the three.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to clear obstructions and hazards as well as manage traffic accidents in tunnels or on bridges administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit's Tunnel and Bridge Commission.

records.text: The Division of Motor Vehicles shall be authorized, at its discretion, to issue written permits authorizing an individual or organization to equip and utilize vehicles with special equipment, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. Such authorization shall permit the use of special equipment on vehicles owned or operated by the permit holder, subject to all applicable laws, Division regulations, and any conditions specified in the permit. The Division may issue such permits upon determining that the proposed use of special equipment is reasonably necessary to ensure the safety of personnel, equipment, or the general public during the performance of official duties or operational functions, or is otherwise deemed necessary by the Division based on unique operational needs or circumstances. Nothing in this section shall obligate the Division to approve any permit application. All permits shall be subject to periodic review and may be modified, suspended, or revoked at the sole discretion of the Division.
The Division shall maintain a current registry of all active permits.

The Division of Motor Vehicles shall have the authority to promulgate rules and regulations necessary to carry out the provisions of this Chapter, including but not limited to defining and clarifying the essential use, operational limits, and display standards of specialized vehicle equipment. Such regulations shall carry the force of law and may be enforced pursuant to 2 M.S.C. §§ 1107 and 1108.

Any individual or organization that operates, or causes to be operated, a motor vehicle equipped with or utilizing special equipment in violation of 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3202, § 3203, § 3301, or § 3302 shall be subject to the penalties established under 2 M.S.C. § 1107. This includes the unauthorized installation, possession, or activation of emergency lights, warning lights, sirens, airhorns, or restricted signal lights without proper legal authority or exemption.

Any individual or organization found to be in violation of a permit condition, regulation, or directive issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to this Chapter shall be subject to penalties under 2 M.S.C. § 1108. This includes, but is not limited to, the improper use, abuse, or misrepresentation of special equipment authorized under a DMV-issued permit.

An individual not holding one of the certificates or licenses outlined in this section may not operate or serve as the pilot in command of an aircraft. The Student Pilot Certificate:
(a) To be eligible for a Student Pilot Certificate, an applicant must ⎼
(i) be enrolled in the Pilot Training Program;
(ii) be physically and mentally able to operate an aircraft;
(iii) not had an airman’s certification or license revoked in the past.
(1) This requirement may be waived by the Administrator for good cause.
(iv) Meet any and all requirements set by the Mayflower Aviation Administration for this certificate.
The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have the authority to promulgate regulations and further criteria pertaining to the Student Pilot Certification.
Applications for a Recreational Pilot Certificate must be submitted to the Flight Standards Office in a form acceptable to the Administrator.
The Private Pilot Certificate:
(a) To be eligible for a Private Pilot Certificate, an applicant must ⎼
(i) Pass the required knowledge certification examination created, dictated, and administered by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.
(1) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have full authority over this examination.
(ii) Receive flight training and an endorsement from an authorized flight instructor under the appropriate guidelines set out by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.
(iii) Pass the practical flight examination created, dictated, and administered by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.

records.text: For the purposes of this chapter, “Aircraft” shall be defined as:
(a) A device or machine that is used or intended to be used for flight in the air.
For the purposes of this chapter, “Civilian Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as:
(a) The person who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of a privately owned Aircraft.
For the purposes of this chapter, “State Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as:

(a) The person, who is an on-duty guardsman or government employee, who is authorised to operate an aircraft and who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of a government owned Aircraft.
For the purposes of this chapter, “Airport” shall be defined as:

(a) An area of land or water that is used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of aircraft, and includes its buildings and facilities, if applicable; this definition shall not refer to or include heliports.
For the purposes of this chapter, “Heliport” shall be defined as:
(a) An area of land, water, or structure that is used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of helicopters, and includes its buildings and facilities, if applicable.

The Port Authority Police Department and Mayflower Transportation Police shall be responsible for determining the security of any government-owned Airport, excluding any Airport within a Military Exclusion Zone.

(a) This shall not prohibit other law enforcement agencies from assisting with or conducting law enforcement duties within an Airport unless otherwise directed by an officer of the Port Authority Police Department or Mayflower Transportation Police.
All Airports shall be considered a Firearm Free Zone.
In any Airport, it shall be illegal to be in possession of—
(a) An item capable of causing harm; or
(b) A facial concealment device.
Law enforcement officers or other security personnel designated by the Secretary of Transportation may search any person who is seeking access to an airport or is within an airport.

Law enforcement officers or other security personnel designated by the Secretary of Transportation may exercise lethal force against any person who is inside or within 50 studs of an airport and possesses an explosive device.
The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall maintain a public database which outlines any property which an aircraft may not fly over.
The Mayflower Aviation Administration may promulgate rules and regulations which dictate—
(a) A minimum altitude requirement for a Civilian Pilot-in-Command when operating an Aircraft;
(b) Areas of the state where an Aircraft may not fly over; and
(c) Areas of the state where an Aircraft may not be within a certain amount of studs of.
It shall be required by law that a Civilian Pilot-in-Command may not operate an Aircraft in the airspace above—
(a) The Capitol Building;
(b) Prison complexes; and
(c) Military Exclusion Zones.

Military or law enforcement personnel shall be authorized to shoot down unauthorized aircraft in restricted airspace by a Senior Officer of the National Guard or a member of the National Guard’s Aviation Unit.

Air Traffic Controllers shall direct pilots and aircraft to avoid protective zones as designated by 3 M.S.C. 1 § 1501, if an aircraft fails to heed warnings of ATC and continues to operate within a protective zone, law enforcement or military personnel establishing the protective zone shall be authorized to shoot down the aircraft.
State Pilot-in-Commands may request exemptions from Flight Codes and No Fly Zones from the Mayflower Aviation Administration.
(a) Government agencies which employ State Pilot-in-Commands may request exemptions on behalf of their State-Pilot-in-Commands.
(b) Approved No Fly Zones exemptions may be referred to as “Temporary Flight Restrictions” and must be publicly accessible through a discord channel.
Any individual who is in possession of an item capable of doing harm or a facial concealment device within an Airport or Heliport shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 3205 "Trespassing."
Any individual who refuses to be searched within an Airport and remains within an Airport shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 3205 “Trespassing."
Any individual who refuses to be searched within a Heliport and remains within a Heliport shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 3205 "Trespassing."
The Mayflower Transportation Police shall be responsible for determining and providing security to any government-owned heliport, excluding any heliport within a Military Exclusion Zone.

(a) This shall not prohibit other law enforcement agencies from assisting with or conducting law enforcement duties within a heliport unless otherwise directed by an employee of the Mayflower Transportation Police or prohibited by a Mayflower Aviation Administration regulation.
All heliports shall be considered a Firearm Free Zone.
In any heliport, it shall be illegal to—
(a) Possess an item capable of causing harm; or
(b) If not an on-duty law enforcement officer or guardsman, possess or wear a facial concealment device (mask).
Law enforcement officers or other security personnel designated by the Secretary of Transportation may search any person who is seeking access to a heliport or is within a heliport.

Law enforcement officers or other security personnel designated by the Secretary of Transportation may exercise lethal force against any person who is inside or within 50 studs of a heliport and possesses an explosive device.
DEFINITIONS. “Tail Number” shall be defined as the combination of letters and numbers assigned to a specific civilian aircraft displayed on the upper sides of a civilian aircraft.
For the purposes of this act, “Registry” or “Registries” shall refer to any database, registry, list, document, or collection containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.

REGISTRY PROHIBITIONS. Notwithstanding 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1401 and 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1601, the Mayflower Aviation Administration may not create any regulation, rule, directive, mandate, order, announcement, or policy forcing owners of civilian aircraft to submit their tail numbers to a registry.
The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not create any registry containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.
(a) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall destroy and erase all registries containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.
(b) The Aircraft Identification Registry and all of its related documents shall be destroyed and deleted.
The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not force any pilot to leak the tail number associated with any civilian aircraft.
(a) All pilots shall enjoy the right of keeping their tail numbers private.
(b) All pilots shall enjoy the right of not having their tail number noted down on any registry.

If the Mayflower Aviation Administration is found violating any contents of this act, the Department of Justice shall investigate the Mayflower Aviation Administration for any findings of registries containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.
